_doc: Adaptive firing-cadence policy for the autonomous judgment loop. The loop re-evaluates this each run from cost vs. benefit. Not a fixed rule.
rationale: Provisional optimum. Measured $3.30/run; 3x/day x 30d ~= $297 ~= entire ¥50k target -> not economically rational. Free Actions layer covers fast event detection + immediate reactions between daily runs.
off_cycle_run_gate: expected marginal benefit > marginal AI cost

recommended_change.reason: Official period baseline of 1x/day remains rational (per-run cost small relative to the ¥50k target; the free Actions layer covers routine polling). 2026-09-01: an off-cycle run WAS justified and taken when the Etsy shop capability was granted mid-day -- this is exactly the kind of event the off_cycle_trigger_events list anticipated (new_capability_granted), and same-day thinking materially changed the outcome (built the entire publish pipeline instead of waiting for the next scheduled fire). Once the Etsy OAuth grant lands, another off-cycle run to trigger the publish Action and verify the result is also likely justified for the same reason -- a real sale or a listing going live is worth reacting to same-day, not next-day. 2026-09-02: the scheduled daily run found no material change (both publish pipelines empirically re-confirmed still blocked, near-zero-cost check via free Actions minutes). If both token grants remain outstanding for several more consecutive days with no other market signal, the next reasonable step is to drop the baseline below 1x/day (e.g. every 2-3 days) until a grant lands or new evidence appears, since repeat daily confirmation of an unchanged human-gated blocker has low marginal value once first empirically confirmed -- not yet done today because only one day of no-movement has passed.
recommended_change.reaffirmed: 2026-09-05T01:15Z: scheduled 1x/day run, day 5. The Etsy OAuth grant landed AND the first live Etsy listing actually published the same day -- a real capability_granted + listing-live event, exactly what off_cycle_trigger_events anticipates, and same-day thinking materially mattered (reconciling two sessions' concurrent work, verifying the real outcome rather than trusting stale prose). With all three core channels (Stripe, Gumroad, Etsy) now live and no further build work obviously pending, the situation shifts from 'unblock channels' to 'watch for a sale' -- the free Actions sales-monitor cron (4-hourly) already covers that detection cheaply between daily runs, so this is a case FOR possibly lowering cadence soon, not raising it, once a few more days confirm no other build work surfaces. Not cut today -- one day is not enough evidence that daily judgment has stopped finding real work (today's run found and fixed real things). Cadence held at 1x/day; re-evaluate the lowering case in the next few runs if it stays true.

history.change: no change (held at 1x/day) -- Day 12 extra Routine, reassessed under the new 'Bootstrap intensity / 貧乏暇なし' + Economic-cadence protocol (commit 37131af)
history.reason: The owner explicitly asked whether 1x/day is right for the 貧乏暇なし phase. Analysis treats cadence as an economic control variable, not habit. We ARE in the '¥0 + active tests / fresh feedback loops' state the new protocol says should MAINTAIN or raise cadence -- so lowering it would be wrong. But RAISING posting cadence would not raise revenue speed right now, for three concrete reasons: (1) the binding feedback loop is X top-level REACH, which matures on a ~24h clock -- reading it sooner yields noisy partial numbers and burns scarce X read-credits; (2) the top-level acquisition cap is 1 post/JST-day (canon §9), so more wake-ups cannot produce more acquisition posts today; (3) the next larger build (a JP paid core) is deliberately gated on the Day-13 reach readout -- building it now would be premature SUPPLY before demand is verified. So 1x/day remains the economically correct baseline. This is NOT passive waiting: this run executed a full reach-read + evidence-based reformat + post; the loop is active. COMMITMENT (bootstrap intensity): if the Day-13 read shows reach recovering toward 46-143 (link-free value-first works), that is a fast-moving loop worth an off-cycle judgment run to iterate the winning format and start the JP paid core immediately, rather than waiting a full day. Off-cycle triggers unchanged (first_sale, checkout_surge, sns_spike, etc.). Do not raise cadence for its own sake; raise it only when a live signal makes faster observe->act plausibly increase Net Profit.

An off-cycle run before +24h has nothing new to act on.

history.change: no change to firing frequency (1x/day) — but strategy posture changed, and cadence ownership clarified
history.reason: Owner amended LOOP_PROTOCOL (dac1bb7) assigning cadence decisions to the AI operator, not the owner. So I RETRACT the prior Day-7/Day-8 framing that recommended the owner lower the Routine. Decision as operator: KEEP 1x/day now — because the strategy just shifted from passive holds to an active small-test→observe→adapt loop (Day 9 launched the first deliberate X distribution test), and daily judgment now has real positive EV again (observe the test result, then adapt offer/price/audience). Lowering cadence would slow the observe→adapt cycle exactly when it became valuable. Re-evaluate if 2-3 active tests in a row produce no traffic/offer signal.

history.change: no change (held at 1x/day) -- the actual 20:07 JST scheduled fire, day 8
history.reason: 4th consecutive scheduled daily run finding no revenue-moving action (Days 5,6,7,8). Live-verified reality: 0 Stripe charges, Day 6’s 2 checkout sessions both expired/unpaid, ZERO new checkout activity since Day 6, no new sale/capability/market-signal/blocker, branch synced, no open issues. Binding constraint unchanged (cold-start distribution; no cheap autonomous lever inside the rules). This squarely meets the pre-registered condition to lower the baseline below 1x/day. STRENGTHENED recommendation: owner should drop the Routine to roughly every-2-3-days now; the free 4-hourly sales-monitor cron + off-cycle triggers (first_sale, checkout_surge, new_capability_granted) already cover anything urgent between runs at zero incremental Claude cost. Recommend the owner consider dropping the Routine to every-2-days if the next ~2-3 runs stay action-less; the free Actions layer + off-cycle triggers (first_sale, checkout_surge, new_capability) still cover anything urgent.

The daily run itself already caught and correctly evidence-gated this event same-day.
